sector_model: commercial stage single product biotech: product revenue concentration, net cash and runway, tax normalization, SBC, pipeline spend and catalysts; not an insurer, bank or REIT model
thesis: Krystal Biotech (Nasdaq: KRYS) sells VYJUVEK (topical gene therapy for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa). Q3 2026 revenue 127.3M (+30%), gross margin 94%, operating income 71.1M vs 41.4M; 9M revenue 362.9M (+28.7%), operating income 183.3M, net income 173.8M (Q3 net income 63.1M vs 79.4M because Q3 2025 had a 31.4M tax benefit). Cash and investments about 1.19B, no borrowings, total liabilities 150.5M; 400M buyback authorized October 2026. TTM revenue 470.0M, net income 225.2M, pretax about 258.8M, OCF 323.9M, capex 13.8M so FCF about 310M, SBC 55.5M so FCF after SBC about 255M. At the verified 2026-11-10 close of 306.50 and 29.63M shares (10-Q cover) market cap is about 9.08B and EV about 7.89B: about 40x TTM GAAP earnings (about 44x at 21% normalized tax), EV about 35x TTM operating income, FCF yield 3.4% (2.8% after SBC). Business quality is high (94% gross margin, net cash, 30% growth) but the price already assumes continued growth and pipeline success; this is a quality lead, not a cheap stock.
counterthesis: Single product concentration (VYJUVEK is all revenue) in an ultra rare disease where the patient pool is finite; Q3 net income fell year over year on tax normalization; TTM tax rate (13%) is below the likely statutory range, so GAAP P/E understates the true multiple. Pretax income includes interest on 1.19B of investments. DOJ subpoenas about the sponsored genetic testing program are an unquantified risk and the company cannot estimate a loss. Customer A is 61% of receivables. Operating margin is already about 56% in Q3, so growth must come from new geographies (Germany and Italy pricing done, launch 2027) and an unproven pipeline (KB111, KB113, KB407; interim data mostly 2027). Stock compensation of 55M TTM is a real cost. At 35x EV to operating income the price leaves little margin for a growth slowdown.
invalidation: Q4 or Q1 VYJUVEK revenue declining sequentially, gross margin below about 90%, an adverse DOJ outcome or a reimbursement change by key payers, pipeline setbacks at KB111 (interim data before year end) or KB407, or cash burn from acquisitions or large R&D increases beyond the 155-165M non-GAAP R&D plus SG&A guide.
